items.title: [Fix] linker: Renew Mooncake read leases that lapse during a load
items.author: alphabetc1
items.summary: The Mooncake direct linker opens get sessions for a load batch and reads it layer by layer. A long batch can outlive the read leases (Mooncake returns ), and the load then aborts every request in it.
items.body:
## Motivation

The Mooncake direct linker opens get sessions for a load batch and reads it layer by layer. A long batch can outlive the read leases (Mooncake returns `-707`), and the load then aborts every request in it. When requests in one batch share a prefix, the same key is read many times in one ranged get, and Mooncake reports the expiry once per key (`-707`) and `-600` for its repeats.

items.author: andakai
items.summary: With them, an EAGLE, EAGLE3 or MTP prefix hit already proves that the draft KV at the block boundary is reusable. The legacy approach drops the last matched block and compensates for it everywhere else.
items.body:
## Purpose

Lookahead block hashes are now used by core prefix caching and by every KV connector. With them, an EAGLE, EAGLE3 or MTP prefix hit already proves that the draft KV at the block boundary is reusable. The legacy approach drops the last matched block and compensates for it everywhere else. It is no longer needed, so this PR removes the drop and makes lookahead hashes the only behavior.

This PR is stacked on #65448, which can enable all connectors lookahead hashes.

items.body:
## Motivation

With the external linker, a Mamba checkpoint taken at a branch point (`mamba_branching_seqlen`) is attached to a node split off an already-stored node. The split node inherits the stored mark, so its Mamba state never reaches the store, and requests that share only that prefix get no L3 hit once the device copy is gone. This affects every hybrid Mamba model served with the linker (e.g. Kimi-K3, Inkling).

HiCache handles the same case through its incremental backup; #48431 adds request-end-only Mamba backups for HiCache and does not touch the linker path.

items.title: [Perf] [AMD] GLM5.3: Run KDA decode and HIP prefill on a BF16 state pool on gfx950
items.author: Raiden-Makoto
items.summary: GLM-5.3-Flash keeps the recurrent state of its 34 KDA layers in FP32 ( resolves to ). Decode and MTP verify are bound by reading and rewriting that state, and the state pool takes GPU memory that the KV cache and prefix cache could use.
items.body:
## Motivation

GLM-5.3-Flash keeps the recurrent state of its 34 KDA layers in FP32 (`mamba_ssm_dtype` resolves to `float32`). Decode and MTP verify are bound by reading and rewriting that state, and the state pool takes GPU memory that the KV cache and prefix cache could use.

`--mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16` already exists, but on gfx950 both fast paths reject a BF16 pool: the row-streaming packed decode (#44659) and the HIP chunked prefill fall back to the generic Triton kernels. This change runs both on a BF16 state pool. All recurrence math stays FP32; only the stored state is BF16.

Under pipeline parallelism, the first PP stage relays every newly received request to the next stage (`_pp_send_pyobj_to_next_stage(recv_reqs)` → `point_to_point_pyobj`, i.e. pickle + gloo send). Every later stage then rebroadcasts the object to its attention TP/CP peers and relays it again.

With `mm_feature_transport=cpu`, `RequestReceiver._finalize_shm_features` has already materialized each image's raw feature tensor into the request object by that point. For example, a 1080p image is about 6 MB of CHW uint8. All of it gets serialized at every hop on the scheduler threads.

#54627 applied `prefill_schedule_interval` to non-DP engines with a separate gate and timing state in the scheduler. Replace that with the mechanism DP already uses: the engine core computes the cadence and passes it to `schedule()` as `throttle_prefills`. Empty `schedule()` calls don't advance the counter, so they can't expire the hold early. Non-DP engines don't run dummy batches, unlike DP ranks, where every loop iteration is a forward pass.

items.title: Fix dataloader checkpoint directory creation on every writing rank
items.author: jwills
items.summary: When external dataloader state is saved per data-parallel rank, only DP rank 0 currently creates the checkpoint's parent directory. A distributed barrier synchronizes ranks but does not guarantee directory visibility across node-local filesystem mounts.
items.body:
When external dataloader state is saved per data-parallel rank, only DP rank 0 currently creates the checkpoint's parent directory. A distributed barrier synchronizes ranks but does not guarantee directory visibility across node-local filesystem mounts. A nonzero writing rank can therefore reach `torch.save` without its parent directory and fail.

Call `ensure_directory_exists` on every rank that writes a state file. Rank-independent loaders retain their rank-0-only writes. Extend the explicit-process-groups regression test, which uses DP rank 3, to assert that the parent directory exists.

items.author: waynehacking8
items.summary: Fixes 32-bit integer overflow in block-FP8 Triton GEMM kernel causing wrong memory accesses when M*K or M*N exceeds 2^31 by switching row offsets to int64.
items.body:
## Overview

`_w8a8_triton_block_scaled_mm` forms its A-row and C-row offsets (`offs_am * stride_am`, `offs_cm * stride_cm`) in int32, so once `M * K` or `M * N` passes 2**31, rows past that bound read A from, and write C to, the wrong address. # What does this PR do?

Widens the block / slot / row offset to int64 in five inference Triton kernels that index a KV block pool or a Mamba state pool. With int32 indices they formed `index * stride` in int32, which wraps once the pool passes 2^31 elements.

- a write or read lands in the wrong block or slot, or

When a prefill KV transfer fails mid-flight (for example, when Mooncake's `batch_transfer_sync` returns `-1` on its wall-clock timeout while the underlying RDMA batch may still be writing to decode's KV pages), the transfer worker calls `poison_deferred_ack_room(room)` (`python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/common/conn.py:1120-1123`) and `conclude_failure()` (`python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/mooncake/conn.py:2883-2890`). Poisoning the room ensures that prefill withholds `ABORT_ACK` so decode holds the destination KV pages until its deferred release timeout rather than freeing them

`media_io_kwargs` is the per-request field that tells vLLM how to load media: `{"video": {"fps": 1}}` samples one video frame per second. items.title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Stream DeepSeek DSML tool-call names and arguments like Python
items.author: james-shore
items.summary: Fixes Rust DeepSeek DSML parser to stream tool-call function names and arguments incrementally, matching Python parser behavior instead of buffering until the closing marker.
items.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

With the Rust frontend, a DeepSeek V3.2 / V4 / V4.1 tool call reaches the client as a single delta after its last token: the DSML tool parser buffers each `invoke` until its closing marker. The Python parser emits the function name when the `invoke` opens and streams the arguments (#58780). This makes the Rust parser stream the same way.

#56334 by @thuanpham582002 fixes the same problem in the same way, and this PR builds on its approach. It was written before four changes to this parser (#56271, #62874, #62875 and #65375) and has had merge conflict

items.title: [Feature] Share a prompt's KV among requests admitted in the same prefill batch
items.author: tianyu-l
items.summary: Requests that share a prompt and are admitted in one prefill batch each compute the whole prompt: the radix cache inserts a request's KV only after its prefill result is processed ( in ), so matches the second and later requests against a tree that does not ha…
items.body:
### Motivation

Requests that share a prompt and are admitted in one prefill batch each compute the whole prompt: the radix cache inserts a request's KV only after its prefill result is processed (`checkpoint_kv_cache` in `process_batch_result_prefill`), so `PrefillAdder` matches the second and later requests against a tree that does not have the first request's prompt yet.

This is the common case for RL rollouts (GRPO-style groups: N samples of one prompt, sent as N requests so each has its own session / routing), and for any client that fans out samples of one prompt as separate requests.

items.title: [Perf][Core] Look up single-group prefix-cache hits with one dict get per block
items.author: davidteather
items.summary: calls once per prompt block until the first miss. For single-group (dense) models that is five Python calls and two allocations per block, on the scheduler thread, on every admission, scaling with the cached prompt length.
items.body:
## Overview

`FullAttentionManager.find_longest_cache_hit` calls `BlockPool.get_cached_block` once per prompt block
until the first miss. For single-group (dense) models that is five Python calls and two allocations per
block, on the scheduler thread, on every admission, scaling with the cached prompt length. This adds
`BlockHashToBlockMap.get_prefix_blocks` (one dict get per block with the group suffix hoisted) and uses
it when there is one KV cache group; multi-group managers keep the existing loop.
`_get_num_evictable_blocks` becomes a list comprehension. Scheduling decisions are unchanged.

Tools frequently define legitimate parameter names that match Python keywords, such as:

items.author: hongxiayang
items.summary: At DCP1, the AMD Kimi-K3 specialized decode refuses to start whenever M1 cannot serve the MLA layers. Kimi-K3.1 (#65685) never qualifies: its DSA layers keep an KV cache, which M1 does not read.
items.body:
## Overview

At DCP1, the AMD Kimi-K3 specialized decode (`decode_backend=latency_specialized`) refuses to start whenever M1
cannot serve the MLA layers. Kimi-K3.1 (#65685) never qualifies: its DSA layers keep an `fp8_ds_mla` KV cache,
which M1 does not read. On ROCm at DCP1, K3.1 therefore gets vLLM's decode only. This PR serves DCP1 without M1
the way DCP8 already does: the MLA layers run vLLM's attention ops, then K2.

## Claims

- **Kimi-K3.1 Pro, ROCm, TP8 DCP1:** the specialized decode now runs. Decode step time is 38% lower at

items.title: [Feature][Hybrid] K0 spec-window slot release for hybrid mamba models
items.author: michael-gpu
items.summary: Releases idle speculative-window KV slots back to the pool at K=0 crossings in hybrid Mamba models, improving throughput by 110% at high batch sizes while reducing peak KV usage.
items.body:
# [Feature][Hybrid] K0 spec-window slot release for hybrid mamba models

## Overview

Hybrid-state (mamba + full-attention) models running MTP speculative decoding keep every request's speculative window allocated even when the dynamic spec-tier table (`num_speculative_tokens_per_batch_size`) resolves the step to K=0 at high batch counts — at a c32 crossing that is most of the pinned KV. This PR releases running rows' idle windows back to the pool at the K=0 crossing, admits waiting rows at the K=0 tier while the pool is pressured (the window born as null row slots), and promotes released rows

items.title: [CPU] Support 2D (batched) weights in rms_norm, fixing DFlash acceptance on CPU
items.author: jimburtoft
items.summary: Fixes CPU rms_norm kernel to support 2D batched weights by selecting weight row by outermost input index, matching CUDA semantics and enabling DFlash speculative decoding acceptance on CPU.
items.body:
## Overview

The CPU `rms_norm` kernel ignores the row dimension of a 2D (batched) weight and applies row 0 to every token. The CUDA kernel selects the weight row by the outermost input index (#46761). DFlash relies on that for its fused per-layer context-key norm (`DFlashQwen3Model._normalize_context_k`), so on CPU every draft layer after the first gets wrongly normalized context keys. This PR adds the same 2D-weight semantics and shape checks to the CPU kernel and enables the existing batched-weight test on CPU.

## Claims

- CPU `rms_norm` with a `[input.size(0), hidden]` weight now match

items.title: [RFC]: Text sessions on /v1/realtime with streaming-input prefill
items.author: AshutoshRautela
items.summary: Proposes adding text-session support to /v1/realtime so non-audio voice agents can stream text into vLLM with resuming-prefill instead of writing custom websocket servers.
items.body:
### Motivation.

`/v1/realtime` is transcription only today. It accepts `input_audio_buffer.*` events and works only for models that implement `SupportsRealtime`. Voice agents that run ASR separately and use a text LLM can't use it.

These agents get the user's words incrementally while the user is still speaking. With streaming input (`StreamingInput`, resumable requests), the engine can prefill those words before the turn ends. When the turn is committed, only the last few tokens are left to prefill before decoding starts. vLLM has this engine support, but the server has no text API for it.

items.author: weimin023
items.summary: On gfx1151, bf16 W4A16 layers fall off a cliff at decode-sized M. Qwen3.8 gateup: 0.7 ms at M=32, 3.0 ms at M=64. [Discussion: Thank you for contributing to the vLLM project.]
items.body:
## Overview

On gfx1151, bf16 W4A16 layers fall off a cliff at decode-sized M.

- At 33-64 rows the Triton tile drops to about 30 GB/s on wide-N layers.
- That is 3-4x slower than the same layer at 32 rows. Qwen3.8 gate_up: 0.7 ms at M=32, 3.0 ms at M=64.
- These M values come from decode batches above the HIP skinny GEMM's 5 rows, and from spec-decode verify steps.

The tiles used there were tuned for prefill. This PR replaces them for bf16 at M 9-128.

## Claims

- Qwen3.8-27B on gfx1151, output throughput:
  - +44% at 64 concurrent requests;
  - +42% and +34% with MTP (k=3) at 12 and 16 req

## Overview

Under adaptive verification, the paged MXFP4 indexer (#58671) scores every decode row of DeepSeek-V4.1 as its own sequence, because its requests carry 1 to next_n query rows and the native path needs next_n each. AITER's paged MQA-logits kernel already takes varlen sequences (`query_start_loc`, as the prefill chunks use), so this plans those decode steps as their requests: a workgroup walks a request's KV tiles once for all its rows.

- On MI355X, the dense decode indexer launches of DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash under adaptive verification take 1.4-2.4x less time: 22.3 -> 15.8

## Motivation

Fixes #48906.

On SM80 to SM9x GPUs SGLang serves NVFP4 linear and MoE layers through FP4 Marlin by default. `nvfp4_marlin_process_scales` turns each E4M3 block scale into an S0E5M3 byte (scale * 2^7, 5-bit exponent with bias 15). items.body:
## Motivation

DFLASH/DSPARK can accept repetition_penalty without applying it during target verification. Restoring one penalty snapshot for the whole block is still insufficient: a token first proposed inside that block must be penalized at subsequent positions, just as in ordinary autoregressive decoding. Under overlap scheduling, CPU Req.output_ids can also omit the previous committed GPU block.

This is a standalone extension of #43207, rebased onto current main. It includes the original penalty plumbing and committed-token accounting by @D1MK4real, plus per-position repetition semantics

items.author: HollowMan6
items.summary: Workaround to avoid Humming's fused-E8M0 path that silently rounds/zeroes MXFP4 weights, falling back to FP16 activations for affected layers; discussion indicates proper fix should go upstream in Humming.
items.body:
## Overview

Fixes #66074.

With FP8 activations (the default for compressed-tensors MXFP4 checkpoints on Hopper), Humming runs MXFP4 linear layers on its fused-E8M0 path. That path keeps only 11 binades of E8M0 scales below the largest scale of the layer's fused weight tensor and silently rounds or zeroes the weights of blocks further down. This PR checks each Humming MXFP4 linear layer once at load time. A layer that would lose weights runs with 16-bit activations instead, which decode the checkpoint exactly, and vLLM logs one warning naming it. Every other layer is unchanged.

items.title: [Doc] Raise the bar for in-tree kernel translation units
items.author: fxmarty-amd
items.summary: Each C++ kernel file in is compiled once per GPU architecture, so a file that instantiates every variant of one op can be the whole build's critical path. Six PRs split the worse ones — #63105, #62716, #62717, #62718, #63364, #63365.
items.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Disclosure

AI assistance was used. The changes were reviewed and tested manually.

## Overview

Each C++ kernel file in `csrc/` is compiled once per GPU architecture, so a file that instantiates every variant of one op can be the whole build's critical path. Six PRs split the worse ones — #63105, #62716, #62717, #62718, #63364, #63365. With them the 9-arch ROCm wheel build goes 85 min 28 s → 472 s, `_rocm_C.abi3.so` 2011.5 → 125.9 MiB, wheel 379 → 266 MiB (#63105, #62921).

Nothing in the repo made that a review criterion, which is what was raised on #63365.

## Motivation

A DeepSeek-V4.1 prefill server can hang on its first busy prefill steps after startup. This happens with DP attention (attention TP 1), `--moe-a2a-backend megamoe`, `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill breakable`, and decoder SWA bounded replay. Every DP rank stops. After 300 s, DeepGEMM's MegaMoE grid-sync timeout traps and the GPUs report Xid 43. A restart doesn't help: the next cold start can hang the same way.

How it happens:

1. With MegaMoE and no DP gather in the graph, `prefill_graph_tolerates_sum_len()` lets each DP rank replay the prefill-graph bucket of its own token count.

items.title: [Multimodal] Add keyframe-aware sampling to PyNvVideoCodec backend
items.author: justincdavis
items.summary: Uniform video sampling picks frame positions without regard to the stream's GOP structure, so reaching most sampled frames means decoding the intermediate frames back to the previous keyframe. On long videos, that decode work is significant.
items.body:
# [MM] Add keyframe-aware video sampling to PyNvVideoCodec

## Overview

Uniform video sampling picks frame positions without regard to the stream's GOP structure, so reaching most sampled frames means decoding the intermediate frames back to the previous keyframe. On long videos, that decode work is significant.

The primary win of this change is a 34% reduction in video decode time across all 900 VideoMME videos, and 56% on long videos.

This PR adds a `keyframe_sampling="nearest"` option to the PyNvVideoCodec video backend. It moves the frame positions chosen by the existing loader

## Description

`GenerationExecutorWorker._shutdown_rank_local()` ends with `gc.collect()` and `torch.cuda.empty_cache()` so that a worker process that outlives its LLM, such as a worker of an MPI pool that hosts successive LLM instances, returns the executor's GPU memory before the next LLM is built in it. Since #19646 the method binds the engine's `local_cleanup` hook to a local variable. The bound method keeps the `PyExecutor` reachable until the method returns, so the collection cannot free the executor's reference cycles, and the model they reference stays allocated after `empty_cache()`.

items.title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Honor and normalize explicit VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT
items.author: yeshihai
items.summary: Normalizes explicit VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT env var to canonical names at config construction time, preventing worker-side cache spec mismatches with HiSparse models.
items.body:
## Overview

HiSparse hybrid models build cache specs in the worker before the engine core resolves the KV cache layout, and workers adopt the engine's layout by name. An explicit `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT` can therefore be invisible during worker-side spec setup, and an alias layout name can make the worker reject the canonical layout.

This applies an explicit `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT` at config construction and stores its canonical name. It is a generic config fix with no model-specific behavior.

Links: #59176 (GLM-5.3-Flash + HiSparse layout mismatch). #61243 is the related open PR adding GLM-5.

Adds an opt-in FSDP engine option, `response_only_lm_head` (default `false`). RL losses read values only at response tokens, but the engine projects every packed token through the LM head. The values at response tokens are unchanged.

In P/D disaggregation with `NixlConnector`, the decode (consumer) could issue the NIXL read of a request whose KV blocks the prefill (producer) had already released and recycled because its lease ran out. This reuses the deadline gate that already protects the bidirectional turn-2 readback and applies it to every remote-prefill read, with an exact model of the lease renewals the consumer's own heartbeats cause.

Level 2 frees GPU memory by not keeping what can be rebuilt, and the only thing rebuilt on wake is what the weight update writes: parameters. Today it discards everything allocated while the model was built, because the weights pool wraps model construction. The rest then has to be rescued one site at a time: buffers by name, and everything held some other way is lost. items.title: [Bugfix][MoRIIO] Let decode renew READ block leases on prefill
items.author: amirakb89
items.summary: Fixes MoRIIO READ mode silently returning wrong output by introducing KV-block lease renewal so prefill does not free blocks before decode finishes reading them.
items.body:
## Overview

In MoRIIO READ mode, prefill frees a request's KV blocks `defer_timeout` (60 s) after the request finishes, even if decode has not read them yet. A request that waits longer than that in decode's queue then reads blocks prefill has already reused, and its output is silently wrong. This PR turns that fixed timeout into a lease that decode renews until it reads the request, following NIXL's KV lease design ([`nixl_kv_cache_lease.md`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/docs/design/nixl_kv_cache_lease.md)).

This is Gap 2 of [ROCm/mori#759](https://github.com/ROCm/mori/iss

items.title: [MFSDP] Bypass gradient packing when inner reduction is unnecessary
items.author: wujingyue
items.summary: When gradients can reach their accumulation placements without inner communication, MFSDP still allocates a packing buffer and copies gradients through it. Accumulate directly into instead, including HSDP/HFSDP with a singleton inner DP axis.
items.body:
- [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

## What does this PR do?

When gradients can reach their accumulation placements without inner communication, MFSDP still allocates a packing buffer and copies gradients through it. Accumulate directly into `main_grad` instead, including HSDP/HFSDP with a singleton inner DP axis.

Each parameter group computes `requires_inner_reduction` from its existing mesh and gradient placements. Groups requiring communication retain the packed path. Other groups accumulate on compute in `main_grad.dtype`, avoiding communication-dtype

items.title: Add an optional TensorAtomic placement for MCore MFSDP v2 dense parameters
items.author: Autumn1998
items.summary: Muon needs each weight matrix whole on one rank to run Newton-Schulz. MFSDP v2 shards the matrices, so today the optimizer step gathers each matrix's pieces to an owner rank and scatters the update back.
items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Muon needs each weight matrix whole on one rank to run Newton-Schulz. MFSDP v2 shards the matrices, so today the optimizer step gathers each matrix's pieces to an owner rank and scatters the update back. This PR adds an optional alternative: with `MFSDP_TENSOR_ATOMIC=1`, every dense parameter stays whole on one owner rank (the `TensorAtomic` placement), so the Muon step needs no gather or scatter. Owners are chosen greedily to balance the Newton-Schulz cost. The plan depends only on parameter shapes, so every rank computes the same one. Experts keep their own mesh.

items.title: [ray] fix: prevent master port races during worker startup
items.author: SeptPonts
items.summary: Prevent during Ray worker startup caused by the gap between selecting a master port and binding PyTorch's TCPStore. Previously, probed a free port with a temporary socket, closed it, and passed the port to workers.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Prevent `EADDRINUSE` during Ray worker startup caused by the gap between selecting a master port and binding PyTorch's TCPStore.

Previously, `RayWorkerGroup` probed a free port with a temporary socket, closed it, and passed the port to workers. Another process could claim that port before rank zero initialized its process group.

Rank zero now binds and retains the actual TCPStore before invoking the user worker constructor. It publishes the bound endpoint before that constructor can block waiting for peers, allowing the driver to start the remaining ranks.

items.title: Fix math_dapo Minerva extraction for markdown-decorated answers
items.author: siddhant-rajhans
items.summary: The existing regex captures the markers as part of the answer, so correct answers score -1.0. Fixes #8449 ## Root cause The Minerva answer pattern matches the literal "Answer" and captures everything after the colon to end of line.
items.body:
## Bug

Models commonly wrap the Minerva `Answer:` label in markdown bold/italic (`**Answer:** 42`, `Answer: **42**`, `**Answer:**\n\n42`). The existing regex captures the `*` markers as part of the answer, so correct answers score -1.0.

Fixes #8449

## Root cause

The Minerva answer pattern `(?i)Answer\s*:\s*([^\n]+)` matches the literal "Answer" and captures everything after the colon to end of line. When models decorate with markdown:

| Input | Extracted | After normalize | Score |
|---|---|---|---|
| `**Answer:** 42` | `** 42` | `**42` | -1.0 |
| `Answer: **42**` | `**42**` | `**42**` |

### What does this PR do?

Starts all distillation teachers at once instead of one after another, which is what dominates startup when the recipe has many teachers.

items.body:
## Problem

For `k3` and `low_var_kl`, `compute_approx_kl` evaluates `exp(x) - 1 - x`, where `x = log_probs_base - log_probs`. This expression is nonnegative in real arithmetic, but subtracting 1 from a float32 exponential can erase the small KL term or make it negative when the policies are close.

### What does this PR do?

Fixes #8433.

`SFTTrainer` built its train/val `StatefulDataLoader`s without a `generator`, so every iterator construction drew a `base_seed` from the global CPU RNG. On resume that draw happens right after the checkpoint manager restores `torch.get_rng_state()`, so the resumed run continued from a different global CPU RNG state than an uninterrupted run. This PR gives each dataloader its own seeded `torch.Generator`, so building iterators no longer touches the global CPU RNG and the restored state is the one training actually continues with.

## Problem

With `--sglang-speculative-algorithm DFLASH` and a colocated rollout engine, the first weight sync silently overwrites the DFLASH draft with target weights. After that, the acceptance length is ~1.0 and rollout is slower than with speculative decoding off.

How it happens:

- slime's colocated sender calls `update_weights_from_tensor` with `serialized_named_tensors`, `load_format="flattened_bucket"` and `weight_version`. It sets neither `selector` nor `disable_draft_model`.

### What does this PR do?

### What does this PR do?

Adds `sharded_nixl`, a checkpoint engine for disaggregated rollout with no trainer-side all-gather. Every trainer rank (FSDP or Megatron) exports only the shards it holds and NIXL-WRITEs them into the rollout workers' staging buffers. Each rollout worker reports what it loads (pipeline stage, resident experts and, for vLLM TP>1, its slice of each tensor) and receives only that. The bucket layout is built on the first sync and cached, so later syncs send no per-tensor metadata. Design: `docs/advance/sharded_nixl_weight_sync.md`.

Use `torch.expm1(x) - x` for k3 KL estimates in the KL penalty, rollout rejection sampling, and off-policy diagnostics. The expression is mathematically equivalent to `exp(x) - 1 - x`, but avoids subtracting 1 from an exponential close to 1.

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

When every rollout in a prompt group gets the same fractional reward, there is no preference between them, so every advantage in the group should be exactly zero. In `_post_process_rewards` the group is centered in float32, and for identical rewards that can leave a residue of about an ulp instead of zero. With std normalization on, the residue is then divided by its own std, which turns it into a small nonzero advantage shared by the whole group.

Small reproduction on current main (a group of 16 rollouts that all scored 0.3, `grpo` with `grpo_std_normalization`):

-

items.title: [Bug] monkey_patch_torch_dist() runs after Megatron binds torch.distributed collectives; segfault in PyWorkHolder::wait on torch 2.13
items.author: ruizhang0101
items.summary: imports at module level (line 11, ) and calls only inside (line 70). binds, and at import time (lines 13 and 35-42), so it keeps the unpatched originals.
items.body:

`monkey_patch_torch_dist()` runs after Megatron has already bound the `torch.distributed` collectives, so Megatron passes `ReloadableProcessGroup` objects straight to torch and every DDP reduce-scatter and distributed-optimizer all-gather goes through torch's `PyProcessGroup` trampoline instead of the patched functions that unwrap the group.

items.author: CharlesXu-HQ

items.body:
## Background

Multi-model SGLang configuration was resolved incrementally while deployment side effects were already being prepared. Invalid topology or ambiguous model entries could therefore fail late, after router or placement setup had begun.

## Problem

The config path did not validate whole-file invariants such as duplicate model names, multiple weight-updated models, complete engine topology, PP/TP consistency, or multi-node divisibility before launch.

## Solution

- Resolve every model and validate the complete config before placement or router startup.
- Reject unknown model fields

items.author: CharlesXu-HQ

## Background

Locally managed SGLang servers are polled through `/health_generate` before rollout initialization can continue.

## Problem

The startup poll had neither a request timeout nor an overall deadline. A hung health request could block startup indefinitely, and failures while waiting left the newly spawned server process tree running.

## Solution

- Add `--sglang-server-startup-timeout` with a positive finite value and a conservative 600-second default.
- Use a monotonic deadline and cap every health request by both five seconds and the remaining startup budget.
- Reject readiness

items.title: fix(rollout): handle nested aborted fully-async results
items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: An aborted leaf inside a fan-out result could therefore enter the completed queue. Requeuing that nested output directly is also invalid because the next generation expects a flat input group.
items.body:
## Background

`generate_and_rm_group` supports custom generation that fans one input out into `list[Sample]`, so a fully-async task can return `list[list[Sample]]`.

## Problem

The done callback inspected only the outer list. An aborted leaf inside a fan-out result could therefore enter the completed queue. Requeuing that nested output directly is also invalid because the next generation expects a flat input group.

## Solution

- Snapshot the flat input group before generation can mutate it.
- Inspect one-level fan-out leaves for `Sample.Status.ABORTED`.
- Requeue the pristine flat snapshot

items.author: shaurya416

items.body:
Fixes #2409

## Problem

`compute_gpqa_reward` falls back to a text match when no option letter can be extracted from the reply. That fallback (1) appended a one-letter gold label as answer text, and (2) searched each candidate as a raw substring of the normalized reply. A reply that never answers, for example `I'm sorry, but I can't help with that.`, therefore scored 1.0 whenever the gold letter (`a`, `b`, `c`) occurred inside a word, and a short numeric choice such as `11` matched inside `2011` or `111`.

## Approach

- A one-character label that is a valid option letter is no longer added t

`MegatronTrainRayActor.init()` backs up the actor and then loads reference, teacher, or old-actor checkpoints into the same model.

items.title: feat(sft): a VL SFT rollout, so a -vl model config can be fine-tuned
items.author: shifangx
items.summary: slime has VL RL and text SFT, and they do not meet. loads a processor at and never refers to it again, its tokens come from the text-only at, and nothing populates.
items.body:
## What

slime has VL **RL** and text **SFT**, and they do not meet. `slime/rollout/sft_rollout.py`
loads a processor at `:37` and never refers to it again, its tokens come from the
text-only `get_loss_mask` at `:49`, and nothing populates `Sample.multimodal_inputs`.
Point a `-vl` model provider at it and the run trains a VL model on text-only batches

## Summary

Fix CUDA autocast from downcasting the FP32 reduction used by VIME's fused PPO entropy path.

Under CUDA autocast, `torch.einsum` can run at a reduced precision even when both operands were explicitly promoted to FP32. The result is saved for entropy backward, so the precision loss affects both the reported entropy value and its gradient.

This change keeps only that CUDA reduction outside autocast and adds a one-GPU regression suite covering FP16/BF16 autocast, masked/unmasked log-prob paths, metric-only/gradient entropy, and chunked/non-chunked execution.

## Background

`_SampleBuilder` heals TITO / chat-template token drift by either REALIGN (overwrite the drifted tail in-place) or FORK (close the builder and start a new Sample). REALIGN is supposed to be a cheap repair of a *short* previous response.

Training and evaluation launch rollout tasks concurrently at three levels: samples within a rollout group, rollout groups within a training batch, and samples within an evaluation batch.

## Fix

items.summary: Enabling KL (--kl-coef 0.1 or --use-kl-loss) without --ref-load used to die in slimevalidateargs with, because it stat'd args.refload before checking it was set. The sibling OPD check just below already guards for None first.
items.body:
Enabling KL (--kl-coef 0.1 or --use-kl-loss) without --ref-load used to die in slime_validate_args with `TypeError: _path_exists: path should be string, bytes, os.PathLike or integer, not NoneType`, because it stat'd args.ref_load before checking it was set. The sibling OPD check just below already guards for None first.

This adds the same guard: ref_load unset now raises a ValueError telling the user to pass --ref-load, and a ref_load that points nowhere still raises the original FileNotFoundError. Two unit tests cover both cases.

Thanks to @kkyyxhll for catching in #2319 that SGLang ignores `sampling_params.temperature` when it computes input/prefill log-probs. items.author: EazyReal
items.summary: That is not a usable on-policy RL policy: the sampling distribution is a delta, while log-probs (and PPO ratios) still come from a softmax. Greedy RL should be rejected at config parse, not assumed away in loss code.
items.body:
## Problem

`--rollout-temperature 0` is greedy decoding. That is not a usable on-policy RL policy: the sampling distribution is a delta, while log-probs (and PPO ratios) still come from a softmax. Greedy RL should be rejected at config parse, not assumed away in loss code.

`--eval-temperature 0` is unchanged; greedy eval remains valid.

## Change

`slime_validate_args` raises if `rollout_temperature <= 0`.

## Test plan

- [x] `tests/test_megatron_argument_validation.py` — `0.0` and `-0.1` raise; existing validate-args cases still pass at the default `1.0`

items.body:
## Summary

Fix IPv6 URL construction in the vLLM engine control plane.

## Problem

The vLLM subprocess requires an unbracketed IPv6 address when binding
the server, while an IPv6 literal must be enclosed in brackets when
used as the host component of an HTTP URL.

Previously, the health-check path could construct an invalid URL such
as:

`http://2001:db8::1:8000/health`

instead of:

`http://[2001:db8::1]:8000/health`

The health check may then keep retrying failed requests, making engine
startup appear to be stuck.

- Reuse the existing `_wrap_ipv6` helpe

## Summary

Replace VIME's custom colocated IPC weight-sync implementation with the native weight transfer engines provided by vLLM and vLLM-Ascend.

This removes the manual IPC handle gathering, serialization, and worker-side chunk loading path while aligning colocated weight updates with vLLM's native `/update_weights` lifecycle.

## What changed

- Use  `NPUIPCWeightTransferEngine` on Ascend to send colocated weights.
- Route native `update_info` payloads through `VLLMEngine.update_weights` and vLLM's `/update_weights` endpoint.
- Initialize the native weight transfer engine once

## Summary

This PR reduces actor-update memory usage when entropy is logged but does not contribute to the loss.

Long-context actor updates can become memory-bound because entropy is evaluated over the full vocabulary. When `entropy_coef == 0`, VIME still computes entropy metrics, but the entropy tensor is only used for reporting and has no gradient contribution. The current implementation always builds the entropy autograd graph and clones the full logits tensor before entropy computation, which increases peak memory without changing the loss.
